title: fix(spec): filter-text-operator-declared-type-refused's control excludes JSON-stored fields and names the JSON-column door
body:
Fixes #21189
Clause-②: no

## What changes

Text only, in one `@objectstack/spec` semantic migration entry: the `acceptanceCriteria` of `filter-text-operator-declared-type-refused` (protocol 18), plus its regenerated region of `packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts` and one `patch` changeset. Neither door's code moves. No entry id, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, conversion or refusal changes either.

The old criteria named every text-valued field as the control that "must keep answering exactly as before". That list included `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags` and lookup and `user` ids. The declared-type door this entry registers does still leave all of those alone. A second door judges a field by how it is **stored**, though, and it now refuses the prefix, suffix, case-folded and pattern operators on a JSON-stored column. So the old sentence named filters that answer `400` after the upgrade as the repair pass's control.

The criteria now say:

- **The control:** a text-valued field that is NOT stored as a JSON column.
- **The JSON-stored population:** `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags`; any field declared `multiple: true` (a multi-valued lookup or `user` among them); and, on a SQL deployment still inside the ADR-0104 dual-encoding window, a single-value file-class field.
- **That door's refusal:** every text operator except the membership pair `$contains` / `$notContains`, with `INVALID_FILTER` / `400`. Its message names no declared type, so these refusals are outside this entry's repair list.
- **The repair:** on a multi-valued field it is membership (`$contains` for one member, an `$or` of `$contains` for any-of), and no rewrite chooses it. A single-value file-class field answers text operators again once the deployment finishes the media-column move (the column step of `objectstack migrate files-to-references --apply`).

## What the text was checked against (`origin/main` at `99692286`, the JSON-column door as commit `2c1cef334` left it)

- **The refused set.** `JSON_COLUMN_INCOMPATIBLE_OPERATORS` in `packages/core/src/utils/json-column-operator-refusal.ts` holds three groups. The equality family is `$eq` and `$ne` with their bare infix spellings. The scalar comparisons are the orderings, `$in` / `$nin` (plus the bare infix spellings) and `$between`. Since `2c1cef334` it also holds `$startsWith`, `$endsWith`, `$icontains`, `$like` and `$ilike`. `$contains` / `$notContains` / `$exists` / `$null` / `$empty` are absent.
- **The refusal.** It is `INVALID_FILTER` / `400` on every face that reads the set. `driver-sql` raises it through `unsupportedFilterError`, and the objectql per-aggregation `filter` through `invalidFilterError`. `driver-memory`'s filter gate reads the same set too.
- **The population.** The engine and `driver-memory` take `STRUCTURED_JSON_TYPES` together with `isMultiValueField`. `isMultiValueField` covers `MULTI_OPTION_TYPES` (`multiselect`, `checkboxes`, `tags`) and any `MULTI_CAPABLE_TYPES` member (`select`, `radio`, `lookup`, `user`, `file`, `image`) declared `multiple: true`. `driver-sql`'s `isJsonField` adds the single-value media family (`FILE_REFERENCE_TYPES`) when `mediaColumnIsJson()` answers true, which means the media columns have not moved.

**The single-value media arm was measured, not inferred.** A throwaway SQLite test through `SqlDriver` (deleted, never committed) covered both arms of the move:

| field | filter | media columns not moved | media columns moved |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `text` | `$startsWith` | rows | rows |
| single `select` | `$startsWith` | rows | rows |
| single `user` | `$startsWith` | rows | rows |
| single `file` | `$startsWith` / `$icontains` | `INVALID_FILTER 400` | rows |
| `select`, `multiple: true` | `$startsWith` | `INVALID_FILTER 400` | `INVALID_FILTER 400` |
| `select`, `multiple: true` | `$contains` | membership rows | membership rows |

The triage direction listed the population as `multiselect` / `checkboxes` / `tags` and multi-valued lookup / `user`. The entry names the population the code holds, which is wider: every `multiple: true` field, and the single-value file classes while the media columns have not moved. Leaving those out would have left the same untrue control sentence for them.

## Tests and gates (all at `3a0bcb2d`, after merging `origin/main` at `62b90d74` through `scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh`)

- **Package build and generated artifacts.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build`, then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec check:generated`, gave "All 15 generated artifacts are up to date". That covers `check:migration-registry`, `check:spec-changes` and `check:upgrade-guide`. The upgrade guide and `spec-changes.json` do not carry this entry's text, so only `registry.ts` moved.
- **Package tests.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run --project local --maxWorkers=2` reported 596 files and 17457 tests passed (1 todo).
- **Typecheck.** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec typecheck` exited 0. `check:test-typecheck` is OK: 52 files, 246 errors, 135 pinned signatures held.
- **Derived gate families.** `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack --commands` derived 82 commands from this tree. Of those, 81 ran with exit 0. `pnpm check:dual-build-cjs-loads` is NOT MEASURED: it exited 3 (PREREQUISITE NOT MET) because it loads every package's built output, and that needs a whole-repo build. CI runs it. The `--ran` reconciliation of the recorded exit codes accounts for all 82 families: 81 run, 1 NOT-MEASURED.
- **Lint, narrowed to the changed files.** The run was `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the two changed `.ts` files. Its JSON output counts 2 files, 0 errors and 0 warnings. Both files fall under `eslint.config.mjs`'s `packages/**/*.{ts,tsx,mts,cts}` blocks. The narrowing is safe because the config never enables type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` and no typed rules, as its own header states). So this diff cannot change the verdict on any file it does not touch.
- **The CLI pin that prints this text.** `packages/cli/test/migrate-meta-engine-guidance.test.ts` spawns the CLI, so it is the integration tier and is declared to CI. It asserts the printed block carries no tracker id. A static grep for `#` followed by 4–5 digits over the entry and the changeset found 0 hits. A positive control of the same regex matched.

## Acceptance notes

- **Not filed: the single-value media arm with `$contains`.** On a SQL deployment whose media columns have not moved, `$contains` with a single-value file field's exact id answered zero rows. The JSON-column door's refusal on that same field prescribes `$contains`. This was measured at the driver only (the SQLite table above, `doc $contains 'fil_one'`), not through a public door, so it is not filed. Carrier: none. It is also why the entry gives that field the media-column move as its repair, not `$contains`.
